notes: The whole arena becomes the boss. Thomas tiles space, so the cubes braid into a fixed set of channels the player can learn — and `period` is the slide: every 6s the field's phase turns a quarter and every channel in the water moves at once. `param` is thomasB, and 0.085 rather than the bait ball's 0.19 on purpose: below about 0.11 the same equations stop settling into a blob and wander a lattice.

The butterfly, with the boss parked on the fixed point between its two wings. Cubes orbit one wing then cross to the other, and when they cross is genuinely unpredictable. `centre` 25 is the picture, not the system — Lorenz's attractor lives around z 25 and this is what puts it on the anchor rather than far above it.

The same system as `release`, viewed down its own axis: a ring, hollow in the middle and fast at the rim. `reach` is the only thing here that moves — world units a second the anchor walks toward the seal, so it CLOSES rather than chases. Two safe places and they are opposites: the hole, or outside the rim. The rolls of cash off the yacht, not the stand-in cube — a closing ring of money is the joke the shape was already making, and a cylinder needs the 0.6 cant or a side view renders it as a rectangle at every angle.

notes: Sensitive dependence as a rule rather than as a look. Cubes arrive in PAIRS seeded a hair apart, travel as one for a few seconds, then end up on opposite wings. `count` is the pair total, so it is half as many events as the number suggests. Wire it to the player's own landed shots and the fight has a dial the player controls. A shoal of glowing fish rather than the stand-in cube. It suits this study specifically: the pairs are seeded a hair apart and read as ONE thing for the first few seconds, which is a shoal splitting rather than a bullet duplicating. Nine bodies, rolled per shot — one repeated fish is a texture. tilt=0 because a fish is already legible side-on and canting it turns the shoal into slivers.

No body-and-bullets split — the cubes ARE the boss and the fixed point at the middle is the only hitbox. `period` is the breath: the cloud contracts until it is a wall, then thins until the core is exposed. thomasB back at the bait ball's 0.19, which is the value that holds a compact mass.

The streamlines are DRAWN in the water first and only then does anything travel down them. That is what lets `speedCap` be twice anything else here: a very fast curved bullet is fair when the curve was shown before the shot. `period` here is the DRAW alone — the length of the telegraph, which is the only half worth tuning; the firing lasts however long the volley needs to walk the shape at `speedCap`. The shape is re-rolled between volleys, so the telegraph is never the same twice.
